text: Twenty-two seconds of rage left, the dome coming down, and Borro back in field form with five fresh minutes.
A car-sized slab falls, and Borro lifts his shield over everyone.
Its weight lands in Jaeha: a hundred and twenty percent, more than he can carry.
The slab shatters, and the rubble buries Borro to the waist. The shield stays up.
Borro is as calm as ever, sweat under his husk face, buried where he stands. Slow things arrive, and slow things stay.
Nib's outline flickers, his knives notched. A scout can do a lot in forty seconds. Not this.
Mok grabs Jaeha's vest and shakes him. The man who sent him in as bait now begs him for a trick.
Past Mok's shoulder, the giant rings on, and the little mark keeps pulsing.
Jaeha's cold private face comes out. He's held one card back since yesterday, just for Mok's raid.
His body will freeze during the call, so Jaeha shoves Mok under the shield and makes him the bodyguard.
Yerin nods hard, hands glowing. Keeping him in one piece has been her job all day.
With a bloody fingertip, Jaeha touches the tiny mark, and it blooms open.
The Call: endless black water, and only one rift open this time, a wide river under a silver sky. One minute to make his offer.
Jaeha faces it, bleeding, silver light on his face.
A woman's laugh carries over the water. She remembers him: the one who read out a job advert.
Jaeha winces at the memory, sweating. He'd hoped nobody over there remembered the ramen.
On a boulder by the river: a tall woman with a long beaded braid, a white bow across her knees.
She glances back with one river-blue eye and a smug half-smile. She'll listen. Barely.
In the corner of the Call, the enrage timer keeps running. Seventeen seconds.
Last time, he tried to guess what they'd like. This time, he simply asks.
She hops up and counts her price on her fingers. Fame and money first, plenty of both.
Then the smile drops. The third request is the one she means: find her missing brother.
Far off, an empty boat is tied to a stilt house. Nobody's there.
He won't lie to her. He offers what he can deliver, the deal that brought Borro through: he'll search, and share the hits.
She taps the bow on her shoulder. Sweet, but she hasn't forgotten items one and two.
Twelve seconds left back in the chamber.
Jaeha jerks a thumb back at the world, grinning through the blood. Applause, he can do: the drone is live.
Her eyes go huge and sparkling. That number does what pretty words couldn't.
She leaps off the boulder straight at the rift, already reaching for an arrow. Sold.
Accepted, nine seconds to spare. Summon number three is coming through, every slot is full, and Route Alignment drops to zero.
Back in the chamber, Jaeha's eyes snap open, and a cyan slit tears open beside the giant's head.
And she makes an entrance, landing on the giant's shoulder in a spray of river water, bow drawn, braid flying, as if the chamber were her stage.
Under the shield, Jaeha goes bright red and looks anywhere else. Nib stares, unimpressed.
Outside, the stream leaps past eight hundred and seventy thousand, and nobody in the chat mentions Mok anymore.
Out in the nave, Sora's needle spins wildly, blazing violet.
Sora laughs out loud. So she's been watching him for Kanghan's Director Baek, who will be thrilled.
Lyra, river archer of the Far Side, summon number three. Mid-battle, her first concern is the camera.
She finds it. In the drone's lens, a tiny Lyra strikes a pose and winks.
Jaeha points her at the only target that matters, with single digits left on the clock.
Then the performance stops. Her eyes go cold and still, aimed point-blank at the crack.
Her arrow streaks straight at it,
and bounces off the bronze with a spark, leaving barely a scratch.
Lyra stares after it, outraged.
Then Nib's amber light goes out. He sinks to one knee, out of the fight for a minute.
The giant swats at its own shoulder, and Lyra flips clear.
She lands on the rim of Borro's shield.
Borro gives her a slow, dry smile from under the rubble. His shield is a popular perch. Lyra has no sympathy.
Seven seconds. Jaeha's eyes move from Borro's shield to Lyra crouched on top of it.
He remembers the aqueduct: Nib on Borro's shield, the force running up into him.
Pass once moved force into a knife. It can do the same for an arrow, and make it heavy.
One hand on Borro's shell, one reaching for Lyra's heel: the giant's next blow will run through Borro, through Jaeha, into her arrow.
Lyra is offended. She has barely arrived, and the merchant thinks he's her boss.
The giant snatches up its clapper and raises it high over their pillar.
Then Mok, unasked, raises his cracked shield beside Borro's. Whatever else he is, he's still a tank.
For a moment, Jaeha just stares at Mok's shield.
Lyra draws to her cheek, the smirk gone, utterly still. One arrow, she swears, is all she needs.
Which is lucky. Only three are left in her quiver.
Under Jaeha's trembling palm, flat on Borro's shell, white-gold light gathers.
His other hand reaches up, fingertips almost touching her heel.
The clapper comes down at the two shields. Lyra crouches at full draw.
The red window: three seconds.
Lyra's eye runs down the shaft to the crack, cold and still.
White-gold light gathers in both his hands as the clapper falls. Everything depends on the instant it lands.
